q: I ______ on a houseboat in Austria since 1988.
e: since + a starting point (since 1988): present perfect, have lived.

q: My cat is a real hunter; she ______ anything that moves.
e: Habit, third person singular, so chases.

q: We ______ the next ECL four weeks from today.
e: Simple future: will + the simple form of the verb (will have).

q: I ______ in the Egyptian Navy for six years.
e: for + a duration up to now takes the present perfect.

q: My teacher ______ to the graduation ceremony tomorrow.
e: A fixed arrangement -> present progressive with future meaning.

q: Both of us ______ a ghost last night on the back stairway.
e: last night -> simple past.

q: My grandkids ______ the Internet right now, so you can't use the phone.
e: right now -> present progressive.

q: Craig and his family ______ in Buenos Aires last year at this time.
e: Plural subject in the past, so were.

q: Your mother ______ from Valencia airport 2 hours ago.
e: 2 hours ago -> simple past.

q: According to the drill instructor, the trainees ______ the barracks right now.
e: Plural subject with right now.

q: I ______ to the Cherry Tree Festival next year in Japan.
e: A settled plan -> be going to.

q: Craig and I ______ to Ireland and ______ the famous Book of Kells.
e: Two completed past actions.

q: There ______ a lot of sniper attacks here in the last three months.
e: in the last three months takes the present perfect, plural.

q: Q: Does your father still live in Lisbon? A: No, he ______ in Norway.
e: Third person singular (he): lives.

q: A: Does your family own a house? B: Neither. My family ______ an apartment.
e: Family is a singular collective, so rents.

q: Q: Does your brother have dimples? A: No, he ______ dimples.
e: Negative of have as a full verb in the present.

q: Surprisingly, the people of that country ______ any gum disease.
e: People is plural, so don't have.

q: Q: Has Petty Officer Vance removed the device? A: No, he ______ removed it yet.
e: Tag question on the present perfect, singular.

q: Q: How much area has the river flooded? A: The river ______ flooded any area at all.
e: Present perfect negative, singular.

q: Q: How many times did he have a score below 60? A: He ______ any scores below 60.
e: The answer repeats the simple past of the question: didn't have.

q: Q: ______ he ever passed the ECL? A: Yes, one time.
e: ever + experience -> present perfect.

q: Q: Does he have to take it again? A: Yes, he ______ to take it again.
e: Tag question on have to, singular.

q: Don't go in that room; Dr. Duffy ______ a patient right now.
e: right now -> progressive.

q: When I arrived home from school, the postman ______ a small parcel.
e: An action earlier than another past action.

q: Everybody ______ going to the dentist.
e: Everybody takes a singular verb.

q: I ______ to the airport tomorrow.
e: Simple future: will + the simple form of the verb (will go).

q: I ______ a good movie last night.
e: "Last night" requires *past tense*.

q: The children ______ right now.
e: right now -> be + V-ing.

q: My friend ______ yesterday.
e: yesterday -> simple past.

q: Every afternoon I ______ to play tennis.
e: I -> like.

q: I promise I ______ study harder.
e: A promise takes will.

q: I ______ in the military for 6 years.
e: for 6 years, up to now: present perfect.

q: By the time you graduate next month, you ______ at least 20 ECL tests.
e: By the time + a future time: future perfect (will have taken).

q: He ______ promoted in 2005.
e: Informal passive with get in the past.

q: My dog ______ cars all the time.
e: Habit, third person singular.

q: Capt. Barrow and his wife ______ in Europe last year.
e: Plural subject in the past.

q: I ______ at DLI since Aug 15.
e: since -> present perfect.

q: Your father ______ two hours ago.
e: ago -> simple past.

q: The privates ______ lunch right now.
e: right now with a plural subject.

q: I ______ Brussels next year.
e: A settled plan -> present progressive with future meaning.

q: Yesterday, I ______ to the movies.
e: yesterday -> went.

q: The next ECL ______ two weeks from now.
e: Simple future of be: will be.

q: By this time next year, I ______ all my exams.
e: By this time next year -> future perfect.

q: While I was driving to work this morning, I ______ about my briefing.
e: Two actions in progress at the same time: past progressive.

q: Before the firemen could extinguish the flames, the house ______.
e: An earlier action in the past.

q: First, I went to the movie; then, I ______ some pizza.
e: A sequence of past actions: simple past.

q: When I was a child, I always ______ my homework.
e: A past habit.

q: Before I went to bed last night, I ______ my teeth.
e: last night -> simple past.

q: Because it was raining, we ______ the picnic.
e: Backshift of tense into the past.

q: I ______ the taste of raw tomatoes ever since I was a little boy.
e: ever since -> present perfect.

q: I need to borrow some money because I ______ to bring my wallet this morning.
e: this morning is a finished period -> simple past.

q: While I was in college, I ______ on most of my tests.
e: A finished period in the past: simple past.

q: You may leave now, unless you ______ to hear the same lecture again.
e: After unless, use the present simple.

q: Just as I was walking into the classroom, the bell ______.
e: A short action that interrupts another one: simple past (rang).

q: I will sit in the car and wait while you ______ in the store.
e: After while with future meaning, use the present simple.

q: Before I could stomp on the brake, I ______ the dog.
e: The past of hit is hit.

q: Because it ______ so much last night, I was unable to play soccer.
e: last night -> simple past.

q: Just as I walked outside, it ______ to rain.
e: Backshift of tense into the past.

q: Before I mail this letter tomorrow, I ______ it.
e: The main clause is in the future.

q: I was sitting in my car when ______.
e: Subject-verb order + simple past.

q: While you are taking the ECL tomorrow, I ______ your papers.
e: An action in progress at a future moment -> future progressive.

q: The policeman shot the suspects before they ______.
e: Past context -> could.

q: My mother ______ the carpet when I got home yesterday afternoon.
e: An action in progress that was interrupted: past progressive.

q: We ______ the flight tickets yet.
e: yet goes with the present perfect negative.

q: I was answering the phone and didn't realize you ______ outside.
e: An action in progress in the past.

q: Deborah ______ a car before she went to New Zealand.
e: Earlier action, so the past perfect of have.

q: By the time they change the law, the damage ______.
e: Future perfect passive.

q: Sony offered Sabine a job before she ______ her degree.
e: An earlier action in the past.

q: I had breakfast quite early, then I ______ to the bus stop and caught the bus.
e: A sequence of actions: simple past.

q: By the end of this year, I ______ enough money to buy a computer.
e: By the end of -> future perfect.
